newsitem.title: SPAIN: NYSE to find potential growth outside US - Grasso.
newsitem.headline: NYSE to find potential growth outside US - Grasso.

text.p: The chairman of the New York Stock Exchange highlighted on Monday the potential for growth of the U.S. bourse via international companies.
"Growth that lies in front of the New York Stock Exchange lies primarily in the international community," Richard Grasso said, addressing a conference at the Madrid stock exchange.
"Internationally our opportunity to grow is limitless," he said.
There was increasing demand for international companies from U.S. investors, providing foreign firms with an opportunity to tap new funds, he said.

"We find ourselves in a period in the U.S. with a growing appetite on the part of...both individual investors and institutional investors to broaden their portfolios to include non-U.S. securities," he said.
At present, international companies make up less than 12 percent of U.S. institutional portfolios, he said. This is expected to double by 2000.
As regards Spain, which at present has seven firms with ADR's listed in New York, the number was expected to increase strongly.
"Here in Spain we estimate that more than 50 companies, some presently traded, some in varying stage of privatisation, will one day qualify to list on the New York Stock Exchange," Grasso said.
Spanish firms traded in New York are Repsol, Telefonica, Banco Santander, Banco Central Hispano, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria and Endesa.
